title: Distinguishing mass from weight
canonical_question: How can you tell mass and weight apart in a problem?
summary: If a value is in kilograms it is a mass; if it is in newtons it is a force, usually weight.
Ask whether the quantity would change on the Moon: mass would not, weight would.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Read the units and the setting
sections.body_md: If a value is in kilograms it is a mass; if it is in newtons it is a force, usually weight. A scale that reads kilograms is really inferring mass from weight assuming Earth gravity. In a moving lift that assumption fails and the reading drifts.

sections.heading: A test you can apply
sections.body_md: Ask whether the quantity would change on the Moon: mass would not, weight would. That single test separates them in almost any problem. Once separated, put mass into F = ma and treat weight as one of the forces.

key_points: Kilograms mean mass; newtons mean force.
Bathroom scales infer mass from weight.
The "would it change on the Moon" test separates them.
core.bridge_to_parent: It gives a practical rule for using mass correctly in F = ma.
